identity.title: First detection of PSR B1259-63/LS 2883 in the millimeter and submillimeter wavelengths with ALMA
identity.journal: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan

paper_type_evidence.quote: We detected radio continuum emission from the binary system in the millimeter/submillimeter wavelengths for the first time.

evidence.quote: The distance to the binary is inferred to be 2.6 kpc (cite: 2018MNRAS.479.4849M).

question.value: Does the pulsar-Be star binary PSR B1259-63/LS 2883 emit at mm/submm wavelengths after periastron, and what do the fluxes imply for synchrotron emission, magnetic field and circumstellar disk emission?

evidence.quote: We report Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) observations of the binary system containing the pulsar PSR B1259–63 orbiting around a Be star LS 2883 after the 2017 periastron passage.
(project code: 2017.1.01188.S)
The data were taken with time division mode (TDM) centered at 97 GHz for Band 3 and 343 GHz for Band 7.

analysis_steps.goal: Constrain B field and electron cutoff

method.value: Equate synchrotron cooling time to time since injection at disk passage (t_p+20 d) to get B and gamma

evidence.quote: Here, we assumed that the electrons were injected when the pulsar passed through the disk around the Be star at $\sim t_{\rm p}+20$ days
If we assume that $B=0.6$ G and $T=64$ days, the Lorentz factor is $\gamma=360$
if electrons are instantaneously injected

method.value: MIRIAD imfit Gaussian fit on Stokes I; 3 sigma upper limits from residual rms

evidence.quote: A Gaussian fit was performed on the Stokes *I* images with the MIRIAD task `imfit`
The data were processed with the CASA/ALMA Pipeline (Pipeline-CASA51-P2B) in a standard manner.

the magnetic field associated with the synchrotron emission is $B\lesssim 0.6$ G
the Lorentz factor is $\gamma=360$

findings_qualitative.value: Band 3 flux unchanged between t_p+71 and +84 days, uncorrelated with GeV flares

evidence.quote: the Band 3 flux did not indicate any time correlation with them

claims.hypothesis: mm emission is synchrotron extension of the radio spectrum

claims.finding: Synchrotron extends to 97 GHz; B≲0.6 G, gamma≳360
